=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:158-159 and 181-189 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: On the partial-publish recovery path (SKIP_VERSION_TAG_CREATE=1), RELEASE_CHECK_HEAD is set to EXISTING_TAG_COMMIT at line 159, and the authorization check at lines 164-170 runs against that value. The stale-tip guard at line 182 compares VERSION_TAG^{commit} (which resolves to EXISTING_TAG_COMMIT) with RELEASE_CHECK_HEAD (also EXISTING_TAG_COMMIT). This comparison is tautological on the recovery path. The script never re-fetches origin/stable after the check completes. If origin/stable advances during the authorization check (which makes GitHub API calls and can take tens of seconds), the script cannot detect it and proceeds to move refs/tags/stable and refs/tags/${MAJOR} backward to the older version-tag commit.
  WHY: A concurrent release or a direct push to origin/stable between the initial fetch at line 77 and the post-check comparison at line 182 would not be detected. The --force-with-lease on the tag push protects against a concurrent tag move, but not against the stable branch advancing independently. The practical window is narrow (between the release check completing and the push completing) and depends on origin/stable advancing during that window, which makes this a NIT-level concern.
- scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:99 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: INSTRUCTION_MARKER_RE is a compiled regex that is defined but never referenced anywhere in the module or test suite. The duplicate-detection logic in check_pr (line 342) uses string containment with INSTRUCTION_MARKER.format(head=head), not regex matching with INSTRUCTION_MARKER_RE. This is dead code with no functional impact.
  WHY: No runtime failure. It could mislead a future reader into thinking the gate parses its own instruction comment markers with a regex.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:lines 181-189 (also lines 158-163) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: On the partial-publish recovery path (SKIP_VERSION_TAG_CREATE=1), RELEASE_CHECK_HEAD is set from EXISTING_TAG_COMMIT at line 159, and lines 173-180 are skipped. The exit-7 stale-tip check at line 182 then compares $(git rev-parse --verify "${VERSION_TAG}^{commit}") against RELEASE_CHECK_HEAD. Because both expressions evaluate to the same EXISTING_TAG_COMMIT value, the comparison is tautological and always evaluates to false. The script never re-fetches or inspects origin/stable after the release check runs on this path. If origin/stable advances on the remote repository during the release check, the script fails to detect the branch movement, bypasses the documented exit-7 guard ("origin/stable moved after the check"), and continues to line 190 where it retargets refs/tags/stable and refs/tags/${MAJOR} to the older version-tag commit.
  WHY: When running mark-stable.sh to recover a partial publish, if origin/stable advances concurrently while the release check runs, the script will not abort with exit 7 as documented. Instead, it proceeds to push the stable and major tags pointing to the stale commit, causing the stable release tags to fall behind the current origin/stable branch tip.
- scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:line 99 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: INSTRUCTION_MARKER_RE is defined as a module-level compiled regular expression but is never referenced anywhere in scripts/protected_path_authorization.py or the test suite. The duplicate instruction comment check in check_pr at line 342 uses string containment on INSTRUCTION_MARKER.format(head=head) rather than regex matching.
  WHY: This is dead code with no runtime failure, but it duplicates INSTRUCTION_MARKER and may mislead maintainers into assuming instruction comment detection uses regex parsing.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

If `origin/stable` advances during the authorization check (lines 164-170, which makes multiple API calls), the script never re-reads `origin/stable` and proceeds to move the stable/major tags backward to the older version tag commit.
